tool: CalculiX ccx 2.21, mesh by gmsh (quadratic tets)
model: one 488x140x6 mm chassis plate extracted from cad/step/gen3/EMOCD_Sled_Gen3.step

load.note: Maxwell attraction between the two Halbach arrays, one plate's share

support_bracket: webs at |y|=48..54 mm; pinned = out-of-plane only (lower bound on stiffness), clamped = all DOF (upper bound). The real joint is between.
conclusion: The chassis plate AS DRAWN meets every declared constraint: 78 % of the deflection budget in the conservative support case, 17x margin on stress, first local mode 17x the requirement. The plate is not strength-driven and is only moderately stiffness-driven.
what_this_does_not_settle: A4 asked for the LIGHTEST chassis meeting the stiffness constraint. This run answers the easier question -- whether the drawn one meets it -- and it does.

Uniform thinning is nearly worthless: deflection scales as 1/t^3, so the budget is exhausted at about 5.5 mm, saving ~0.30 kg of the 9.445 kg sled and moving exit velocity from 16.53 to about 16.7 m/s.

Real mass reduction needs a rib-stiffened redesign, where section depth enters as the square. That is design work this analysis does not evaluate, and it means the 60 % pocketing row in docs/DESIGN_OPTIONS_exit_velocity.md is NOT supported by anything yet.
idealisations: One plate in isolation, not the assembled box.
Web attachment idealised as two support lines; the bracket is pinned vs clamped.
Load applied as equal nodal forces over the footprint rather than the consistent quadratic-face load vector. Total force is exact; local distribution is approximate.
Magnets bonded to the plate would stiffen it locally -- not modelled, conservative.
Static Maxwell attraction only. No launch loads, no arrest event, no thermal.
verdict: pass on all three declared bands for the as-drawn plate. The sled mass question stays open, and the decision rule's >=6.80 kg branch stands: at 9.445 kg the machine delivers 16.53 m/s.
